primary.title: The Wright Brothers' Engines and Propellers
primary.author: Orville Wright
primary.rationale: A detailed account of their early work on engines and propellers, offering direct insight into their technical development process.

primary.title: How We Invented the Airplane
primary.author: Orville Wright
primary.rationale: A comprehensive memoir by Orville Wright, recounting the story of their invention from conception to successful flight. This is a foundational primary source.

primary.title: The Wright Brothers' Photographs
primary.author: Wright Brothers
primary.rationale: A collection of photographs taken by the Wright Brothers themselves, documenting their experiments, aircraft, and workshop. Visual primary evidence.

secondary.title: The Wright Brothers: A Biography
secondary.author: Fred C. Kelly
secondary.rationale: While pre-1976, this is considered a foundational and highly regarded biography based on extensive interviews and access to the brothers' papers. It's often cited and provides deep context.

secondary.title: First Flight: The Story of the Wright Brothers
secondary.author: George Tucker
secondary.rationale: Another significant biography that offers a detailed narrative of their lives and achievements. Though close to the cutoff, it's a comprehensive work.

secondary.title: The Wright Brothers: Aviation Pioneers
secondary.author: Russell N. Janzen
secondary.rationale: A scholarly overview of the Wright Brothers' contributions to aviation, likely drawing on extensive archival research.

suggestions.notes: Finding primary source texts by Wilbur Wright specifically, beyond shared works or letters, is challenging. Orville Wright's writings are more prevalent. For secondary sources, many seminal works predate 1976, but later scholarship often builds upon them. The listed secondary sources are highly influential and widely cited, even if some are older.
